diagnostics.advice.curl: Updates fall back to allow_url_fopen. Fine if that is on.
diagnostics.advice.data_hidden: Open data/settings/config.php in a browser. You should get 403 or 404. Apache reads the .htaccess Pluck ships; nginx ignores it, so those rules have to be in the server config — see NGINX.md.
diagnostics.advice.disk: Under 100 MB free. When an account fills up the site stops, not only the backups — lower how many backups are kept.
diagnostics.advice.intl: Dates show as 2021-06-01 rather than 1 June 2021.
diagnostics.advice.mail: The contact form keeps every message on the site, but cannot e-mail them to you. Ask whether mail() is available.
diagnostics.advice.media_inert: Put a file called probe.php in media/ containing an echo, open it, and check it comes back refused rather than run. Delete it afterwards.
diagnostics.advice.memory: Under 64 MB. Backups of a large media folder may not finish.
diagnostics.advice.outbound: Pluck cannot check for updates. Ask whether outgoing HTTPS is allowed, or watch the releases page yourself.
diagnostics.advice.post_smaller: post_max_size is below upload_max_filesize, so larger uploads are cut off before Pluck sees them and nothing can report it.
diagnostics.advice.pretty_urls: Addresses look like ?page=about rather than /about. Switch it on under Settings; Pluck checks first and refuses if rewriting does not work.
diagnostics.advice.required_extension: Pluck cannot run without this one.
diagnostics.advice.session_owner: Some session files belong to another user, so signing in appears to work and bounces back to the form. Usually a migration run as root: chown -R www-data:www-data data/ — or your host’s own web user. Pluck removes the one blocking your own sign-in, but the rest stay until somebody clears them.
diagnostics.advice.sessions: Signing in cannot work without this, and it fails by looping back to the form rather than saying anything. Usually: chown -R www-data:www-data data/
diagnostics.advice.sqlite: Only flat-file storage is available. That is fine for most sites.
diagnostics.advice.time: Under 30 seconds. A backup or an update may be cut off halfway.
diagnostics.advice.writable: Give the web server write access to this folder. If you installed or migrated from a shell, the files are probably owned by the wrong user.
diagnostics.advice.zip: Theme and module archives cannot be read. Backups are unaffected — those are tar.
diagnostics.advice.zlib: Backups are written uncompressed. They work; they are just larger.
diagnostics.flash.owners_only: Only an owner can see the diagnostics.

diagnostics.help.intro: What Pluck needs and what this server provides. Where they differ, the last column says who can change it — you, or the company hosting the site. The wording is meant to be pasted into a support message.

update.blocked.fix: This is almost always an install unpacked by hand as another user. Give the files back to the account the site runs as:
update.blocked.fix_hosting: The folders can be written but the files cannot, so PHP runs as one account and the files belong to another. Do not chown everything to the web server — that takes the files away from you. The fix belongs on the server: run PHP as the account that owns the site, with a PHP-FPM pool of its own. As a stopgap you can make the files group-writable:
